//: THE BUDGETS ARE ENFORCED BY `replay/tools/build_browser_bundle.mjs`, WHICH FAILS THE BUILD.
A number in a comment is not a budget. This file is data the builder reads and
`verify_browser_replay_dd9_clean` re-reads, so the two cannot come to disagree about what was
promised.
WHAT `eager` MEANS, precisely, because it is the whole point: an entry output plus the transitive
closure of its STATIC (`import-statement`) edges. An output reached only by a `dynamic-import`
edge is LAZY — the browser fetches it when the code path runs and not before. esbuild marks split
targets with `entryPoint` too, so `entryPoint` is NOT the discriminator; using it would count 8.3
MB of lazily-fetched barretenberg as eager.
TWO BUDGETS, BECAUSE THEY ARE TWO DIFFERENT PROMISES.
`library` is `src/index.ts` — what a consumer pays to USE the replay client.
`page` is `browser-demo/replay_in_page.ts` — what a USER LOADS. It additionally carries
`ct-host` and the browser AVM loader, which a library consumer does not, so summing them would
make one number a statement about neither. The page is the thing a person waits for, so it is
budgeted rather than merely reported.
WHY THESE NUMBERS. Measured 2026-08-30 AFTER the DD-11 poseidon substitution landed — set after,
deliberately, so they pin the state actually wanted rather than the one being left. Library
1,087,168 in 5 chunks; page 1,116,208 in 5. Each ceiling is ~10% above its measurement: loose
enough that ordinary churn in `replay/src` does not fail a build, tight enough that the
regressions worth catching are caught. They are CEILINGS, not targets.
AND THE BYTE BUDGETS ARE THE WEAKER GUARD, DELIBERATELY — for both entries. The regression that
matters is STRUCTURAL: one of the two 4 MB barretenberg blobs becoming eagerly imported. A byte
budget catches that only incidentally, by being smaller than 4 MB. `lazyRequired` names those two
directly, so the property is ASSERTED rather than inferred from a size, and it is checked against
BOTH entries' closures. DD-11's demand is about WHICH CHUNK a module is in, not about how many
bytes there are — and `smoke_browser_replays_settled_transaction` §5 carries the other half of
it, that the page fetches none of them at run time.
`maxEagerFiles` exists so a NEW eager chunk is visible even when it is small. Five chunks
totalling 1.1 MB and six totalling 1.1 MB are different facts about the graph.

measured.note: Before the poseidon substitution the page FETCHED 4,139,020 bytes of barretenberg at run time. It now fetches none; the blobs remain in the graph as lazy chunks that nothing reaches.
